The Shang Dynasty bronzes marka defining moment in Chinese culture. The craftsmen developed and refined a process thatallowed themto produce largebronzevessels of unparalleled quality.The process, called piece-mould casting, employed an unusual alloy, adding lead to the normal mix of copper and tin. During casting the surface ofthe vessels couldbe adorned with fantastic, animal-like imageryand motifs, which may have been relatedto ancient sacrificial or funerary rites.

The creation of the Terracotta Army for the tomb of Qin Shi Huang is equallyremarkable, but for different reasons. This wasanearly example of mass-production. Standard moulds werecreated forthe mainbodyparts: there wereeight different torsos, two types of leg,eight faces,and so on.
